Replicated measurements are needed to assess variation; short timing differences are limited evidence.

claims.statement: The optional operator guide correctly groups allocations (new_zeros, empty/new_empty/empty_like), views (view/unsqueeze/as_strided), embedding lookup (index_select), attention softmax, FFN GELU, and matrix-product work (mm/matmul/addmm).
claims.location: 16.1 second and third paragraphs of profiler operator optional detail; main matrix row explanation
claims.scope: new_zeros fills zero; empty family allocates uninitialized values under this default configuration, which must not be read as meaningful data. The three views share storage here; index_select performs lookup, softmax acts over attention keys, GELU is the FFN activation. mm/matmul multiply and addmm also adds input. These are operation categories, not unique layer labels.

evidence.locator: new_empty L118-L149; new_zeros L217-L248; view L6041-L6087
evidence.supports: Uninitialized allocation, zero-filled allocation, same-data view semantics.

evidence.locator: empty/empty_like L12680-L12750; unsqueeze L12475-L12495; as_strided L1019-L1052; index_select L5563-L5588; mm L7831-L7850; matmul L7908-L7948; addmm L592-L620
evidence.supports: Full coverage of remaining allocation/view/index/matrix operator semantics; default empty exception for deterministic fill explicitly acknowledged in scope.
ATen embedding implementation actually calls index_select for both word and position embeddings.
Softmax normalizes the selected axis and GELU is elementwise.
TinyLM uses last-axis softmax and QK/weight-V matrix products.
TinyLM default FFN actually uses GELU.
Executed storage-pointer, indexing, row-sum, shape and explicit 2x2 matrix assertions without reading uninitialized values.

verification.details: Related APIs verified as one coverage group, with each family linked to its official source and actual model mapping.

claims.statement: Keeping the model fixed and replacing ids with torch.arange(1,13)[None] yields (1,12,264), unchanged weight bytes. Repeating each length three times with 3 warmups/5 captured forwards and comparing the same operator name can produce the allowed no-stable-difference result.
claims.scope: Six bounded CPU profiles of a single model; actual rows preserved. No general assertion that longer input is faster/slower and no whole-model bottleneck inference.

evidence.supports: Input position length propagates to logits; sequence does not alter model parameter tables.
Six executed captures, lengths 3/12, three trials each; parameter state bitwise unchanged, no gradients/updates.

sort_by and row_limit select/sort display without changing aggregated operator identity.

verification.observed: All shapes/bytes exact. mm calls=25, matmul=35, addmm=10 in each five-forward capture. Self CPU times vary; no stable increase at length 12. Weights bitwise unchanged; grads absent; updates=0

claims.statement: Parameter payload bytes cannot represent peak runtime memory: inference has intermediate features and generated cache; training also stores gradients and optimizer state. Profiling itself has overhead, so use it to locate work and separately repeat timing for total cost.
claims.scope: Memory categories and measurement limitations, not a numerical TinyLM peak-memory/speed benchmark or a universal fixed overhead percentage.

evidence.supports: Training memory categories include parameters, activations, gradients, optimizer state and intermediates.
K/V tensors are saved as new_cache, separate from parameter payloads.
Intermediate embeddings/features/logits and returned cache exist during inference.
Profiler-internal host overhead is recognized in official implementation.
Warmup and replicated timing account for initialization and run variability.
